items.title: Ringgit extends gains against US dollar as traders reassess Fed rate outlook
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The ringgit extended its gains to close higher against the US dollar today as traders reassessed the possibility of an interest rate hike by the US Federal Reserve (Fed), an analyst said. The Fed decided to keep the benchmark interest rate steady at 3.75 per cent to 4.00 per cent on Oct 28. At 6 pm, the ringgit rose to 4.0555/0600 against the greenback from yesterday’s close of 4.0575/0620.

items.title: Mi Technovation buys Singapore building for RM332mil
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Mi Technovation Bhd is buying a seven-storey industrial building in Singapore for RM331.8 million to establish a global operational hub for its vehicle technologies business. In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the company said the proposed acquisition would support the expansion of its vehicle technologies business unit (VTBU). Mi Technovation said the property would serve as VTBU's future Singapore headquarters and global operational hub.

items.title: NSTP booth draws crowds at Jom Heboh with 600 free newspapers daily
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Crowds have flocked to The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd (NSTP) booth at Karnival Jom Heboh (KJH) Johor Baru 2026, attracted by its daily distribution of 600 free newspapers and a range of interactive activities. NSTP Branding and Intellectual Property Department head Tengku Kaifimirza Tuan Cherit @ Tengku Hamzah said the sponsors' participation reflected their continued commitment to supporting NSTP's community-based programmes. Also present was NSTP Branding and Intellectual Property Department senior officer Wan Fazly Hizam Wan Kadir.

items.title: Police open two investigation papers after Kluang LED screens hacked to show obscene videos
items.summary: KLUANG: Police have opened two investigation papers following reports that eight light-emitting diode (LED) screens installed around the town were hacked and used to display obscene videos yesterday. Kluang police chief Assistant Commissioner Bahrin Mohd Noh said police received a report from a 42-year-old man today. "The complainant received several messages via WhatsApp containing screenshots and videos of the obscene content displayed on the LED screens.

items.title: Sabah defence upgrades not a response to Philippine military build-up, says Khaled
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 30 — Malaysia will continue strengthening its military capabilities in Sabah to safeguard national security amid regional geopolitical developments, but the move is not a direct response to the Philippines’ military build-up on Balabac Island, Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. “Every country has the right to strengthen its military capabilities, and Malaysia will do the same. Khaled said strengthening Malaysia’s defence capabilities, particularly in Sabah, remained a key priority of the Defence Ministry.

items.title: The more, the merrier? State Pakatan chairman says crowded Melaka races could work in coalition’s favour
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — Pakatan Harapan (PH) does not regard multi-cornered contests in the Melaka state election as a disadvantage, saying a crowded field could instead create more opportunities for the coalition to secure victories. Melaka PH chairman Adly Zahari said a straight fight did not necessarily give a party an advantage, as three- or four-cornered contests could, in certain circumstances, offer better prospects from a strategic standpoint. Also present was Melaka PKR chairman Adam Adli Abd Halim.

items.title: MOF never ordered rural road projects cancelled, only deferred new contracts, says Tengku Zafrul
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The Finance Ministry (MOF) has never issued any directive to cancel rural road projects, but has only deferred new contracts to prevent outstanding payments to contractors from continuing to accumulate, according to the prime minister’s senior political adviser, Tengku Datuk Seri Zafrul Tengku Abdul Aziz. He said the deferment was necessary following rural road development expenditure exceeding the original allocations approved by Parliament annually since 2022, resulting in increased contractual commitments and outstanding payments to contractors. “In Sabah and Sarawak alone, actual rural road expenditure this year reached RM1.41 billion, the highest in the past 10 years.

items.title: AAPA: Asia Pacific airlines carry 30.4mil international passengers in September
items.summary: Air cargo demand grew 6.4 per cent, according to preliminary figures from the Association of Asia Pacific Airlines (AAPA). AAPA director general Wong Hong said passenger numbers increased following five consecutive months of year-on-year declines with stronger growth in longer-haul travel and international air cargo demand. International passenger demand, measured in revenue passenger kilometres (RPK), increased 5.9 per cent year-on-year, while available seat capacity expanded 6.8 per cent.

items.title: UEM Sunrise, AME Elite team up for RM4bil industrial park
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: UEM Sunrise Bhd and AME Elite Consortium Bhd have formed a 50:50 joint venture to develop a 162.7-hectare industrial park in Gerbang Nusajaya, with a gross development value (GDV) of RM4 billion. The joint venture company Gerbang Synergy Sdn Bhd will buy the freehold land from UEM Sunrise's unit Nusajaya Rise Sdn Bhd for RM972.1 million. The partnership combines UEM Sunrise's landbank and township planning capabilities with AME Elite's industrial park development expertise and multinational client network.

items.title: Anwar directs agencies to address e-commerce complaints from consumers, traders
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed agencies to take immediate action to address complaints from consumers and traders over various issues involving e-commerce platforms. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive had been issued to the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry and the Communications Ministry, particularly the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC). "He has asked the relevant ministries and agencies to take action on several issues, particularly fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms," he said at a post-cabinet press conference.

items.title: Roblox taps Malaysia's Joel Neoh to lead Southeast Asia, Oceania
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Roblox has appointed Malaysian entrepreneur Joel Neoh as managing director for Southeast Asia and Oceania as the global gaming and creation platform looks to expand its presence in the regions. Roblox said Southeast Asia and Oceania offer significant long-term growth opportunities, supported by their young, digitally savvy populations and rapidly evolving digital ecosystems. Neoh brings two decades of experience founding and scaling technology businesses across Asia Pacific, covering digital media, e-commerce, financial technology, consumer health and artificial intelligence.

items.title: Nestlé, Red Crescent ready 7,000 flood aid packs
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Nestlé Malaysia and the Malaysian Red Crescent (MRC) have prepared 7,000 flood aid packs worth about RM1.8 million to support families in flood-prone communities as the monsoon season approaches. The annual Nationwide Flood Aid Relief initiative marks the fourth consecutive year of collaboration between Nestlé Malaysia and MRC. In Sabah, employees from Nestlé's local operations, Harrisons Sabah and MRC Sabah worked together to prepare the additional aid bags.

items.title: Mahadev Shankar: A life devoted to justice, integrity and public service
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than two decades ago, the late former Court of Appeal judge Datuk Mahadev Shankar wrote that death would be meaningless if it did not put life into perspective. In a tribute today, Malaysian Bar president Anand Raj described Mahadev as a towering figure whose contributions extended far beyond the courtroom. Anand said Mahadev was widely respected for his sharp judicial mind, mastery of languages and unwavering commitment to justice.

items.title: Saris, sweets and shopping sprees: Deepavali buzz builds across Malaysia
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The festive atmosphere ahead of Deepavali on November 8 is becoming more vibrant as the Indian community nationwide begins making preparations for the Festival of Lights, including purchasing traditional attire, preparing special delicacies and decorating their homes to celebrate the occasion with family and relatives. Another visitor, N. Rama Rao, 38, said Little India remains his family’s preferred shopping destination as it offers a wide selection of traditional attire at reasonable prices. Shoppers browse traditional attire, accessories and festive decorations ahead of Deepavali in Johor Bahru October 30, 2026.

items.title: MCA gets fourth seat as BN takes Kota Laksamana from PN
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: MCA will contest four seats in the Melaka election after securing Kota Laksamana, a constituency initially allocated to Perikatan Nasional (PN). MCA announced the additional seat in a Facebook post today, naming Melvin Chua Kew Wei as its candidate for Kota Laksamana. However, Kota Laksamana was subsequently allocated to MCA, reducing PN's share to five seats.

items.title: Sabah rural road projects must proceed, says Ewon
items.summary: PENAMPANG: The 13 rural road projects in Sabah whose Letters of Acceptance (LOA) have been deferred must still be implemented, said Penampang member of parliament Datuk Ewon Benedick. He said clarification was needed on the status of the projects, including whether they had been cancelled or postponed to the following year. "As the Penampang MP, I want an explanation on the status of the 13 projects whose LOA have been deferred.

items.title: Coffee shop association urges crackdown on illicit cigarettes
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysia Singapore Coffee Shop Proprietors' General Association (MSCSPGA) has called for stricter and more frequent enforcement against retailers selling illicit cigarettes. The association said illicit cigarettes remained easily accessible in many neighbourhoods, with sales allegedly involving foreign workers operating retail outlets. Citing a Wawasanex survey conducted in May, MSCSPGA said 68.8 per cent of illicit cigarette buyers identified migrant workers as the main sellers, while 99 per cent said illicit cigarettes were easy or very easy to obtain.

items.title: RM5bil China loan redirected to Perak water project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government has repurposed RM5 billion of loans from China to finance a major water supply project in Perak, turning part of the financial liability from two abandoned pipeline projects into funding for essential infrastructure. The RM5 billion, originally linked to the Trans-Sabah gas pipeline (TSGP) and multi-product pipeline (MPP) projects which were terminated in 2018, was redirected towards the northern Perak water supply scheme (NPWSS). The Finance Ministry said the move converts part of the financial liability arising from two abandoned pipeline projects into funding for essential water infrastructure.

items.title: Rubbish raid! Thirteen-foot crocodile caught after rummaging through trash for food in Sarawak village
items.summary: KOTA SAMARAHAN, Oct 30 — A crocodile measuring over 13 feet (about 3.96m) was captured this morning following reports of the reptile roaming in the area and posing a potential safety concern for nearby villagers. Licensed crocodile capture team Sarawak Crocter said in a Facebook post that the operation was carried out in collaboration with the Sarawak Forestry Corporation (SFC). — The Borneo Post

items.title: 2027 Penang Budget: RM500 aid for newlyweds among new state initiatives
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Newlyweds in Penang will receive a one-off RM500 cash incentive next year under a new initiative aimed at expanding the state's social safety net. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow announced the initiative, known as the "Mempelai Emas" programme, when tabling the 2027 Budget at the state legislative assembly. The marriage incentive is among several new welfare measures and initiatives announced for next year.

items.title: Bought one thing, got another? Anwar orders crackdown on online shopping scams, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry (KPDN) and the Communications Ministry, through the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC), to take immediate action against fraud and scams on e-commerce platforms. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the directive followed Anwar’s concerns over problems faced by online shoppers and sellers, including high commission fees imposed on merchants and customers receiving products that did not match their orders. “The prime minister raised concerns about the problems faced by e-commerce users, particularly high fees and commissions charged to sellers, as well as customers receiving products that differ from what they ordered.

items.title: Govt studying policy to declassify historical documents
items.summary: Unity Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the Cabinet had agreed with views put forward by several historians on the need for such a policy. He said the government would consult the Attorney-General's Chambers, Home Ministry and police on several related aspects. However, he said no specific timeframe had been set for implementing the declassification process.

items.title: High Court: JMB cannot impose outright ban on pets in residential units
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: A joint management body (JMB) cannot impose an outright ban on keeping pets in private residential units through its house rules, the High Court ruled today. In a statement, they said the court declared that House Rule 9.0 could not be used to prohibit Noraseela from keeping her three cats in her unit. It said any enforcement action must instead be based on By-law 14 of the Strata Management (Maintenance and Management) Regulations 2015 and supported by evidence linking the particular animal to an alleged nuisance, danger or other prohibited circumstance.

items.title: Penang tables RM1.074b budget, forecasts record-low RM5.62m deficit
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government today tabled an operating budget of RM1.074 billion for 2027, projecting a deficit of RM5.62 million — the lowest shortfall in the state's fiscal history. Non-revenue receipts are projected at RM277.79 million, while tax revenue is expected to contribute RM224.94 million. This is followed by emoluments at RM231.8 million (21.58 per cent), services and supplies at RM219 million (20.38 per cent), other expenditure at RM11.38 million (1.06 per cent) and asset acquisitions at RM4.32 million (0.4 per cent).

items.title: Public varsities allowed to hold online classes for Deepavali break
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: Public universities, polytechnics and community colleges have been allowed to conduct online or hybrid teaching and learning (PdP) sessions from Nov 5 to 13 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration on Nov 8. In a statement today, the Higher Education Ministry (Mohe) said the arrangement would allow Hindu students and teaching staff to return to their hometowns and spend time with their families during the festival. Mohe also extended its Deepavali greetings to all Hindu students, academic staff, ministry personnel and Malaysians.

items.title: Tabung Kasih@Hawana aid eases burden of NST journalist recovering from accident
items.summary: IPOH: New Straits Times (NST) journalist Zahratulhayat Mat Arif, who was injured in an accident with Bernama journalist Nur Afiradina Arshad last Sunday, has expressed gratitude for financial assistance from Tabung Kasih@Hawana x TM. Zahratulhayat, 37, said the contribution would help cover the costs of medical rehabilitation and psychiatric consultations following the accident on Jalan Ipoh-Lumut. Also present were Perak Media Practitioners Association chairman Sayed Mohd Hesham Idris and deputy chairman Abdul Razak Mohd Ali.

items.title: Repairs on Kuching’s Jalan Lapangan Terbang water main completed, supply restoration in stages, says Sarawak Water
items.summary: KUCHING, Oct 30 — Emergency repair works on a critical 750mm mild steel cement-lined (MSCL) water main on Jalan Lapangan Terbang were completed at 2am today, said Sarawak Water Sdn Bhd. The utility provider said water supply restoration is now underway in stages. Following completion of the repair works at 2am, Sarawak Water said valve reopening and network pressurisation had commenced, with water supply expected to be restored gradually.

items.title: Sale of first industrial plots on Silicon Island to start in Q1 2027, says Penang CM
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — The Penang government hopes to sell the first industrial plots on Silicon Island as early as the first quarter of 2027, said Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow. He said the development on Silicon Island will focus on the 700-acre Green Tech Park which is planned as a green, smart and sustainable high-tech industrial hub in line with environmental, social and governance (ESG) principles. He said the first factory in the Green Tech Park is expected to begin operations by 2028 while creating high-skilled employment opportunities for Penangites.

items.title: Singaporean fan makes annual Karnival Jom Heboh trip despite mobility challenges
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: A stroke in February did not deter a loyal Singaporean TV3 fan from attending Karnival Jom Heboh 2026 at Padang B, Angsana Johor Bahru Mall here today. Jannah Naz Abdullah, 50, said she has never missed attending the iconic carnival since its inaugural edition in Bukit Jalil, Kuala Lumpur, in 2003. "I came from Singapore solely to attend KJH.

items.title: Indonesian woman fined RM4,000 and ordered deported over RM100 sex offer to undercover cop in Kuching
items.summary: Magistrate Nureina Syafika Mohd Najib imposed the sentence against Pita, 37, after she pleaded guilty to a charge under Section 372B of the Penal Code. During the inspection of an unnumbered room, police found Pita with the undercover agent and arrested her for further action. Investigations found that Pita had offered sexual services to the undercover agent for a cash payment of RM100.

items.title: Penang civil servants to receive one-month bonus in December
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: Penang civil servants will receive a special financial assistance equivalent to one month's salary, payable in December, the state legislative assembly was told today. Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow said the incentive was a token of appreciation for the dedication and integrity demonstrated by the state public sector workforce. Chow said one-off payments of RM300 would also be given to supervisors and teachers of Quran and Fardu Ain (Kafa) classes, staff of Islamic religious primary and secondary schools, government-aided religious schools, tahfiz and pondok institutions.

items.title: Penang Budget 2027 sets aside RM600 aid for e-hailing drivers, RM500 for newlyweds
items.summary: “This is for eligible drivers in 2027 with an allocation ceiling of RM9 million,” he said when tabling the Supply Bill at the state legislative assembly today. He said the state government had disbursed RM57.8 million through the implementation of the first and second phases of the i-Sejahtera programme as at September 30. “As such, in 2027, the Penang State Housing Board (LPNPP) will explore the co-living concept for suitable state government rental housing and People’s Housing Programme units,” he said.

items.title: Cabinet agrees to amend guidelines to speed up abandoned vehicle disposal, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Cabinet has agreed to amend the guidelines on the management of abandoned vehicles to speed up the process of removing and disposing of such vehicles, following complaints over delays and poor coordination among enforcement agencies. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the proposed amendments were put forward by the Housing and Local Government Ministry (KPKT) and Transport Ministry (MoT) after taking into account various feedback and complaints about the existing procedures. He said the current process could take too long and required better coordination among the agencies involved.

items.title: RM30 million allocated for Media Innovation Fund 2.0
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The government has allocated RM30 million for the Media Innovation Fund 2.0 to support the transformation and growth of the local media industry. Government spokesman Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the initiative would help media companies strengthen their operations and explore new approaches to content production and delivery. "The Madani government will continue the Media Innovation Fund initiative through the implementation of Media Innovation Fund 2.0, with an allocation of RM30 million.

items.title: Penang tables RM1.07b Budget 2027 with record-low RM5.62m deficit
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Oct 30 — Penang Chief Minister Chow Kon Yeow today tabled a RM1.074 billion budget for 2027, with a projected deficit of RM5.62 million. He said the estimated deficit was the lowest in the state’s budget history, compared to the projected deficit of RM19.92 million for 2026. He said the budget included a contribution of RM240 million to the state development fund, compared to RM265 million in 2026.

items.title: Two Penampang road upgrades worth RM173m running ahead of schedule, says Ewon
items.summary: PENAMPANG, Oct 30 — Two rural road upgrade projects in Kampung Buayan and Kampung Terian here, involving a total allocation of RM173.263 million, are making positive progress, with both projects ahead of their scheduled completion timelines. Sabah deputy chief minister III Datuk Ewon Benedick said the RM73.868 million Kampung Buayan rural road upgrade — involving a 5.6-kilometre stretch of road and the construction of two bridges — is at 76.64 per cent physical progress, 45 days ahead of schedule, and is expected to be completed in August 2027, while the RM99.395 million Kampung Terian rural road upgrade — involves a 6.7-kilometre stretch of road — is at 57.83 per cent progress, 58 days ahead of schedule, and is expected to be completed in May 2028. He hoped that both rural road projects, together with other small-scale development projects, would improve infrastructure facilities and benefit residents and visitors to nearby villages once fully completed.

items.title: Govt to begin declassifying historical documents under Official Secrets Act, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The government is expected to declassify historical documents, particularly those classified as official secrets under the Official Secrets Act, as soon as possible, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim raised the matter during the second 2026 National Historians Council meeting held earlier this week. “The Cabinet agreed with several views put forward by historians on the need to establish a general policy on the declassification of historical documents currently classified as official secrets under the Official Secrets Act.

items.title: Affordable books key to nurturing young readers in Sabah
items.summary: KOTA KINABALU: Making books more affordable and accessible is key to encouraging children to develop reading habits, think critically and explore new ideas. Sabah Chief Minister's special officer Yee Tsai Yiew said access to books could help shape the next generation by encouraging children to question, imagine and broaden their understanding of the world. Big Bad Wolf Books Kota Kinabalu 2026, featuring more than one million books, runs until Nov 9.

items.title: Melaka MACC opens 24-hour operations room ahead of election
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) in Melaka will set up a 24-hour operations room to receive public information and complaints on corruption and abuse of power during the Melaka election. "The public may submit any information or complaints throughout the election process via email at prnmlk@sprm.gov.my, by contacting the MACC Melaka office line at 06-2896000, the operations room at 06-2896303, or the 24-hour hotline/WhatsApp number at 011-26791569," the statement read. MACC also reminded all candidates, political parties, supporters and other parties involved in the 16th Melaka election to refrain from actions that violate election laws and regulations, in accordance with the MACC Act 2009 and the Election Offences Act 1954.

items.title: Classic Land Rover Defender associated with Cameron Highlands to get new lease of life as tourist vehicles
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Classic Land Rover Defender vehicles associated with Cameron Highlands could continue operating as tourist vehicles despite exceeding the usual 15-year age limit under a new Transport Ministry policy. In a statement, the ministry said the vehicles could be considered for use as Cameron Highlands Iconic Tourism Vehicles (KIPCH), provided they meet specified safety requirements, technical standards and licensing conditions. The ministry said the classic Land Rover Defenders were suited to Cameron Highlands’ hilly terrain and challenging routes, particularly for off-road tourism activities.

items.title: Deepavali: Higher Education Ministry allows online or hybrid classes from Nov 5 to 13
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Higher Education Ministry (MOHE) has allowed online or hybrid Teaching and Learning (PdP) sessions to be conducted at public higher education institutions from November 5 to 13 in conjunction with the Deepavali celebration on November 8. The ministry also extended its Deepavali greetings to all Hindu students, academic staff, ministry personnel and Malaysians. “May this Festival of Lights bring happiness, peace and prosperity to everyone,” MOHE said.

items.title: Melaka polls: Fence-sitters hold key to victory, says Rafizi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The outcome of the Melaka election is likely to be determined by fence-sitters rather than avid supporters of any political party, says Parti Bersama Malaysia (Bersama) leader Datuk Seri Rafizi Ramli. He said supporters of each major coalition were estimated to make up only a relatively small proportion of the electorate. Based on current estimates, Rafizi said, Barisan Nasional supporters account for about 20 to 21 per cent, Pakatan Harapan 18 to 19 per cent, and Perikatan Nasional 17 to 18 per cent.

items.title: Selangor Immigration Dept repatriates 83,787 foreigners, collects RM42.6m in 17 months
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Oct 30 — The Selangor Immigration Department (JIM) has successfully facilitated the repatriation of 83,787 foreign nationals under the Migrant Repatriation Programme (PRM) 2.0 from May 2023 to September 30. Selangor Immigration Department acting director, Mohmad Khusairi Kamarudin, said this achievement over the 17-month period represents the highest number of registrations and applications recorded compared to other states. “During the same period, the Selangor Immigration Department (JIM Selangor) also successfully collected over RM42.6 million, consisting of more than RM1.68 million in special pass fees and nearly RM41 million in compounds,” he said during a press conference at Selangor JIM headquarters here today.

items.title: MCMC awarded RM15.3mil liquidated damages over delayed Sabah Jendela project
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The High Court in Shah Alam has ordered a contractor to pay RM15.32 million in liquidated damages to the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) for failing to complete works under the National Digital Network (Jendela) project in Sabah within the agreed timeframe. The court also ordered MajuBina Resources Sdn Bhd to pay RM5,000 in costs to MCMC. MCMC said all communications infrastructure projects funded through the USP fund must comply with contractual obligations and agreed timelines.

items.title: More than 6.5 tonnes of chicken seized over suspected halal violations in Puchong
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: More than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with halal certification standards were seized during a midnight raid on a Puchong warehouse yesterday. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department Wildlife Crime Control Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid, conducted at 12.40am, uncovered premises suspected of being used to slaughter, process, and distribute fresh chicken without valid halal certification. Zaki said authorities seized 468 plastic packages containing raw chicken weighing approximately 6,555kg, with an estimated value of RM85,400.

items.title: Malaysian man, Vietnamese wife get 30 years for 173kg meth trafficking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — The High Court today sentenced a couple to 30 years in prison after finding them guilty of trafficking 173kg of methamphetamine four years ago. “The court finds that the prosecution has successfully proven its case beyond reasonable doubt and finds both accused guilty and convicted on the charge,” she said. Deputy Public Prosecutor Goh Ai Rene sought a heavy sentence, citing the quantity of drugs involved at 172.74kg.

items.title: Domestic helper who punched autistic boy 23 times, recorded abuse jailed in Singapore
items.summary: SINGAPORE, Oct 30 — A 29-year-old Indonesian domestic helper has reportedly been sentenced to three years in jail for abusing a four-year-old autistic boy in her care, including punching him at least 23 times despite his attempts to protect himself. According to Singapore’s CNA , the woman, whose identity cannot be disclosed to protect the victims, also kicked the boy’s head twice in a separate incident and recorded videos of her employer’s children naked. Investigations subsequently uncovered four videos and two photographs showing the children naked in the toilet, with the woman having sent two videos and both photographs to her husband, CNA reported.

items.title: Home Ministry: Refugee registration card not a path to Malaysian citizenship, PR or permanent stay
items.summary: KDN said any employment access granted to DPP holders is temporary and limited, and subject to conditions and government approval. “DPP is also not an incentive or pull factor for new refugees to enter Malaysia. At the same time, KDN said lawful employment access would enable refugees to acquire skills, experience and verifiable employment records.

items.title: Penampang road upgrades to improve access to 3 schools
items.summary: PENAMPANG: Three schools in Penampang will benefit from road upgrades in Buayan and Terian, with both projects progressing ahead of schedule, said Datuk Ewon Benedick. The Penampang member of parliament said the improved roads would benefit SK Terian, SK Buayan and SK Longkogungan, located about 12km away, as well as about 3,000 residents in four villages. "There are two schools in this area, namely SK Terian and SK Buayan.

items.title: Cabinet approves UUCA amendments to lift curbs on students’ freedom, new law planned
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The Cabinet today approved proposals to amend the existing Universities and University Colleges Act (UUCA), particularly provisions seen as restricting students’ freedom of expression and association, said Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil. He said the Cabinet also agreed to develop a new law that would eventually replace the UUCA entirely within a reasonable timeframe. “In December, God-willing, the Higher Education Minister will table amendments to the existing UUCA,” he said.

items.title: Heavy rain forecast for east coast, Johor and Sarawak until January
items.summary: PUCHONG: Kelantan and Terengganu are expected to experience continuous heavy rain in November, followed by Pahang and Johor in December, and Sarawak in January, the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) said. Its National Weather and Earthquake Operations Centre senior director Maqrun Fadzli Mohd Fahmi said three to five episodes of continuous heavy rain were expected between November and January during the early phase of the northeast monsoon. In March, Kelantan, Pahang, Labuan, Sabah and Sarawak are expected to receive slightly below-average rainfall.

items.title: Nadma advises public against panic buying ahead of north-east monsoon
items.summary: PUCHONG, Oct 30 — The public has been advised against panic buying or excessively stockpiling food amid concerns over the 2026/2027 Northeast Monsoon (MTL), and instead to make preparations according to their respective needs. National Disaster Management Agency (Nadma) director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said the spread of unverified information, particularly on social media, could trigger panic buying, potentially leading to other problems, including disruptions to the supply of goods. “Sometimes, panic buying creates another problem, not a Northeast Monsoon disaster, but a shortage of goods instead.

items.title: Nadma warns unprepared, low-risk areas pose biggest threat this monsoon
items.summary: Its director-general Datuk Meor Ismail Meor Akim said areas accustomed to flooding generally had better response mechanisms in place, while less frequently affected areas might be less prepared. We pray the forecast is right," he said. In new areas, I'm more worried," he said.

items.title: Melaka polls: Fire Dept conducts safety checks at nomination, vote-tallying centres
items.summary: MELAKA, Oct 30 — The Malaysian Fire and Rescue Department (JBPM) has inspected 28 nomination and official vote-tallying centres ahead of the 16th Melaka state election. Melaka JBPM director Mohd Zaidi Ma’at said the inspections were conducted at the request of the Election Commission (EC) to ensure that fire safety facilities at the centres were in good working order. “The inspections cover fire safety systems and emergency exits to ensure that safety at nomination and polling centres is given due attention.

items.title: Govt, parties to jointly monitor reform commitments under Bersatu CSA, says Fahmi
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Oct 30 — The development allocations provided for reforms under the confidence and supply agreement (CSA) will be monitored jointly by the government and the parties that signed the agreement, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said. He said the monitoring would follow a mechanism established under the previous CSA, which involved joint assessments by both parties to determine whether the agreed commitments had been fulfilled. “The government intends to fulfil the commitments made under this CSA, particularly those involving institutional reforms.

items.title: Two charged with posting extremely offensive comments against Tuanku Muhriz on social media
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — Two men pleaded not guilty in the Sessions Court here today to charges of creating and posting extremely offensive comments against Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, on social media in August. The accused, unemployed Abdullah Aidid Mochtar @ Ahmad Duta, 44, and graphic designer Ashadi Zul’izzi Zainal Abidin, 46, entered the plea after the charges were read before Judge Muhammad Ilmami Ahmad. Abdullah Aidid is accused of creating and initiating the transmission of extremely offensive communications with intent to offend through the TikTok account “rookiebenz_albenzauto” at 11.27pm on August 1, while Ashadi Zul’izzi is accused of the same act via the Threads account “razakahmad725” at 2.39pm on August 4.

items.title: Kluang council shuts down LED screens after obscene video appears in suspected hack
items.summary: KLUANG, Oct 30 — The Kluang Municipal Council (MPK) will investigate an incident where its public message LED display system in several locations were hacked, resulting in displaying an obscene video last night. The municipal council said it has since lodged a police report to facilitate further investigation into the embarrassing incident. MPK also apologised for any inconvenience caused to the Kluang community following the incident.

items.title: Malaysia takes delivery of first two South Korean FA-50M fighter jets
items.summary: LABUAN, Oct 30 — Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin today received the first two FA-50M light combat aircraft acquired by the Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF), marking an important milestone in the country’s efforts to strengthen its air defence capabilities. The two aircraft, developed by Korea Aerospace Industries (KAI), arrived today at RMAF Labuan base, after being flown from Sacheon, Republic of Korea. “The 18 FA-50M aircraft were procured under Malaysia’s Fighter Lead-In Training and Light Combat Aircraft programme, following the planned decommissioning of the RMAF’s Hawk aircraft in 2028,” he said.

items.title: Puchong halal raid nets 6.5 tonnes of chicken allegedly scalded before slaughter, 12 foreign workers held
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 30 — More than 6.5 tonnes of raw chicken suspected of being processed without complying with Islamic slaughtering requirements and halal certification standards were seized during a raid on a warehouse in Puchong here shortly after midnight yesterday. Bukit Aman Internal Security and Public Order Department (JKDNKA) Wildlife Crime Control Bureau/Special Investigation Intelligence (WCB/PSK) commander Datuk Mohd Zaki Ashar said the raid, conducted at 12.40am, uncovered premises suspected of being used to slaughter, process and distribute fresh chicken without valid halal certification. He said preliminary inspections revealed slaughtering and handling practices that raised serious concerns over compliance with Islamic requirements and the halal status of the products.

items.title: Adat Perpatih must be preserved and documented for future generations, says N. Sembilan MB
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Oct 30 — Adat Perpatih, a matrilineal customary law system practised predominantly in Negeri Sembilan, must be preserved and documented through digital technology, academic publications and heritage education to ensure the state’s cultural traditions are not lost over time. Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim said safeguarding the heritage was not solely the responsibility of customary institutions and museums, but required the involvement of communities, educational institutions and government agencies. “Adat Perpatih is more than a set of inherited customs.
